headline: Union Home and Cooperation Minister Shri Amit Shah today inaugurated and laid the foundation for development projects worth ₹6,453 crore across 17 districts from Alwar, Rajasthan.
fullText:
Ministry of Home Affairs

Union Home and Cooperation Minister Shri Amit Shah today inaugurated and laid the foundation for development projects worth ₹6,453 crore across 17 districts from Alwar, Rajasthan.

Today, from a single platform, our government has provided Kisan Samman Nidhi to farmers, a ₹500-crore dairy infrastructure initiative for cattle rearers, jobs for the youth, and expansion of Saras Dairy for the benefit of mothers and sisters

If India is to become a fully developed nation by 2047, we must empower four pillars—youth, the poor, farmers and women. The Modi government is working with this resolve

Cooperative dairies have the potential to transform the rural economy and open new doors of opportunity for the next generation

Through Saras Dairy, the dairy farmers of Rajasthan will receive payment for their milk within just seven days

Cooperative dairies have the power to transform the rural economy, Prime Minister Modi is committed to ensuring that not a single village remains untouched by the cooperative movement

From 2014 to 2026, there has not been a single year in which Prime Minister Narendra Modi did not launch a major initiative for farmers and livestock owners

Under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi, the Government of India has procured the highest-ever quantity of foodgrains at Minimum Support Price (MSP)

Modi government is making every village in the country prosperous through the cooperative movement

We will realise Prime Minister Modi’s vision of “Sahakar Se Samriddhi” and make every village prosperous

Today, the foundation stone has been laid for a milk-processing plant in Alwar with a capacity of 3 lakh litres per day, Its capacity will soon be increased to 5 lakh litres

Four Saras Dairy plants are also being commissioned today in Bhilwara, Jaipur, Pali and Rajsamand at a total cost of ₹274 crore

16 AUG 2026 9:32PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for development works of the Rajasthan Government worth ₹6,453 crore in Alwar, Rajasthan. Rajasthan Chief Minister Shri Bhajan Lal Sharma, Union Minister Shri Bhupender Yadav and several other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

Addressing the gathering, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that if India is to become a fully developed nation by 2047, the youth, the poor, Annadata (farmers) and women must be empowered. Today, farmers here are receiving Kisan Samman Nidhi; dairy infrastructure worth ₹500 crore is being created for livestock rearers; jobs are being provided to the youth; and Saras Dairy expansion works are being undertaken for mothers and sisters.

Shri Amit Shah said that Bhoomi Pujan for a 3 lakh-litre milk processing plant was performed in Alwar today. He said its capacity would soon be increased to 5 lakh litres. When 5 lakh litres of milk every day is supplied by poor livestock rearers to the dairy and the money reaches their bank accounts, it transforms the fortunes of the entire family.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that the cooperation and dairy sectors have immense potential to transform the rural economy, improve the lives of poor livestock rearers and open up a host of opportunities for their future generations. We want to take high milk-yielding breeds of cows and buffaloes to every household across Rajasthan, including Alwar. He said Rajasthan Chief Minister Shri Bhajan Lal has taken steps to insure livestock. Shri Shah said that opportunities for the export of milk products would also emerge in the coming days.

Shri Amit Shah said that, apart from Alwar, four Saras Dairy plants worth ₹274 crore are becoming operational today in Bhilwara, Jaipur, Pali and Rajsamand. Along with this, four district banks are also being launched today in Phalodi, Balotra, Didwana-Kuchaman and Pratapgarh. Farmers will receive loans at zero percent interest from all these banks. Today, ₹152 crore under the Chief Minister's Crop Insurance scheme has been transferred through DBT. More than ₹667 crore has been disbursed to 67 lakh farmers under the Mukhyamantri Kisan Samman Nidhi at the rate of ₹1,000 per farmer. In addition, foundation stones were laid and Bhoomi Pujan was performed today for 954 works with a total cost of ₹6,453 crore. He said that works worth ₹5,500 crore were launched in Chittorgarh this morning, and now works worth ₹6,453 crore have been launched here. Thus, Bhoomi Pujan for development works worth ₹11,953 crore has been performed in a single day today.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that Rajasthan currently has 44,000 cooperative societies. He said our goal is to ensure that not a single village in the State remains without a cooperative. Shri Shah stated that 50 new warehouses are scheduled to be constructed in 2026–27, while 62 warehouses with a capacity of 100 MT and 100 warehouses with a capacity of 500 MT have already been completed.

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has announced a scheme for farmers and livestock rearers every year: the Gokul Mission in 2014; Krishi Sinchayee Yojana and Soil Health Card in 2015; Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana and e-NAM in 2016; Kisan Sampada Yojana in 2017; 1.5-fold MSP in 2018; PM Kisan Samman in 2019; Agriculture Infrastructure Fund and Matsya Sampada Yojana in 2020; establishment of the Ministry of Cooperation in 2021; Kisan Samriddhi Kendras in 2022; International Year of Millets in 2023; National Mission on Edible Oils in 2024 and Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana in 2025. He said that not a single year from 2014 to 2026 has passed without Prime Minister Modi launching a major initiative for farmers.

Shri Amit Shah said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government of India has made the highest procurement of foodgrains at Minimum Support Price. Prime Minister Modi has increased the MSP of bajra by 130%, mustard by 103%, wheat by 84%, cotton by 120% and jowar by 168%.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that Prime Minister Modi's goal is to make every village in the country prosperous through the Ministry of Cooperation. By translating into reality the cooperative mantra of 'Sahkar se Samriddhi' given by Prime Minister Modi, we will make every village prosperous.

RK / RR / PR / PS

summaryText:
### OVERVIEW
Union Home and Cooperation Minister Shri Amit Shah inaugurated and laid foundation stones for development projects worth ₹6,453 crore across 17 districts in Alwar, Rajasthan, focusing on farmer support, dairy infrastructure, youth employment, and cooperative expansion.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- Development projects worth ₹6,453 crore launched across 17 districts from Alwar, Rajasthan
- ₹500 crore dairy infrastructure initiative announced for cattle rearers
- Kisan Samman Nidhi provided to farmers; ₹667 crore disbursed to 67 lakh farmers at ₹1,000 per farmer
- ₹152 crore transferred through DBT under Chief Minister's Crop Insurance scheme
- Foundation stone laid for 3 lakh litre-per-day milk processing plant in Alwar, with planned expansion to 5 lakh litres per day
- Four Saras Dairy plants commissioned in Bhilwara, Jaipur, Pali, and Rajsamand at cost of ₹274 crore
- Four district banks launched in Phalodi, Balotra, Didwana-Kuchaman, and Pratapgarh offering zero percent interest loans
- Bhoomi Pujan performed for 954 works costing total of ₹6,453 crore
- Additional development works worth ₹5,500 crore launched in Chittorgarh same day, totaling ₹11,953 crore in single-day launches
- Rajasthan has 44,000 cooperative societies with goal of covering every village
- 50 new warehouses planned for 2026-27; 162 warehouses already completed (62 at 100 MT capacity, 100 at 500 MT capacity)
- Annual farmer initiatives listed from 2014-2026 including Gokul Mission, PM Kisan Samman, Ministry of Cooperation establishment, and Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana
- MSP increases cited: bajra 130%, mustard 103%, wheat 84%, cotton 120%, jowar 168%
